summary: This week brought fresh congressional interest alongside persistent questions about government transparency and witness protection. New UAP footage reportedly shifted at least one lawmaker's skepticism, while lawmakers continued pushing for release of the 1952 Washington DC UFO encounter tape as the FY2026 NDAA briefing deadline passed. Luis Elizondo, a central figure in UAP disclosure efforts, recalled warnings from congressional staff about plans to "eliminate" him, underscoring broader concerns raised by UAP experts that whistleblowers lack adequate legal protections from retaliation. The Defense Department continued withholding core evaluation details on national security grounds, even as AARO released new technical analyses on satellite flaring and observation parallax. Meanwhile, disappearances of two government officials with apparent UAP connections and unconfirmed speculation about Elon Musk's knowledge of classified programs added unusual dimensions to the week's discourse.
